label: Conceptual Definition and Economic Rationale
info: Integrated multi-modal infrastructure networks designed to connect industrial production clusters with ports, consumption centers, and transport corridors. They shift planning from fragmented project-based interventions to spatial regional economic zones, accelerating industrial clustering, logistics cost reduction, and manufacturing-led urbanization.

label: Macroeconomic Impact on Logistics Costs
info: Economic corridors serve as the core vehicle to lower India's national logistics cost from historical highs of ~13–14% of GDP down to global benchmark levels below 8–9%, boosting export competitiveness and integration into Global Value Chains (GVCs).

label: Apex Governance Framework: NICDIT
info: Governed by the National Industrial Corridor Development and Implementation Trust (NICDIT), an apex body established under the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT), Ministry of Commerce and Industry. Chaired by the Union Minister of Commerce and Industry.

label: Implementation Architecture: NICDC and SPV Structure
info: National Industrial Corridor Development Corporation (NICDC) acts as the operational knowledge partner and project development agency. Individual industrial nodes are executed via joint Special Purpose Vehicles (SPVs) formed on a 50:50 equity basis between the Government of India (through NICDIT) and respective State Governments, leveraging State Support Agreements (SSAs) and Shareholder Agreements (SHAs).

label: Key Flagship Reports and Atlases
info: National Industrial Corridor Programme Annual Status Reports (NICDC/DPIIT); Logistics Ease Across Different States (LEADS Report by DPIIT); PM GatiShakti National Master Plan Monitoring Platform; and World Bank Logistics Performance Index (LPI) country assessments.

label: National Industrial Corridor Development Programme (NICDP) Scale
info: Encompasses 11 designated industrial corridors covering 32 greenfield smart industrial nodes/cities across four phases, designed with 'plug-and-play' advanced trunk infrastructure, high-speed rail-road linkages, and pre-cleared environmental approvals.

label: Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (DMIC) - Profile
info: India's pioneering industrial corridor, spanning 1,504 km across six states (Uttar Pradesh, Haryana, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Gujarat, and Maharashtra). Conceived with financial and technical backing from the Government of Japan (JICA/JBIC).

label: DMIC Transportation Backbone and Nodes
info: Anchored directly along the Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC). Houses landmark smart city and manufacturing nodes, including Dholera Special Investment Region (DSIR, Gujarat), Shendra-Bidkin Industrial Area (AURIC, Maharashtra), Vikram Udyogpuri (MP), Integrated Industrial Township Greater Noida (IIT-GN, UP), and Jodhpur-Pali-Marwar (Rajasthan).

label: Amritsar-Kolkata Industrial Corridor (AKIC)
info: Spans roughly 1,856 km across seven states (Punjab, Haryana, Uttarakhand, UP, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal). Aligned with the Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (EDFC) to revitalize traditional agrarian and manufacturing heartlands. Key nodes include Rajpura-Patiala (Punjab), Hisar (Haryana), Khurpia (Uttarakhand), Agra-Prayagraj (UP), and Gaya (Bihar).

label: Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (CBIC)
info: Developed with bilateral cooperation from JICA to link southern automotive, electronics, and aerospace manufacturing zones across Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, and Karnataka. Priority industrial nodes include Krishnapatnam (AP), Tumakuru (Karnataka), and Ponneri (Tamil Nadu).

label: Bengaluru-Mumbai Industrial Corridor (BMIC)
info: Runs along National Highway 48 through Maharashtra and Karnataka, intended to link India's financial capital with the southern technology and biotechnology hubs. Major emerging industrial node under implementation is the Dharwad Industrial Area in Karnataka.

label: East Coast Economic Corridor (ECEC) & VCIC
info: India's first coastal economic corridor, spanning ~2,500 km from West Bengal to Tamil Nadu, structured with analytical and financial support from the Asian Development Bank (ADB). Phase-1 is the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC) in Andhra Pradesh, featuring nodes at Visakhapatnam and Chittoor (Srikalahasti-Yerpedu).

label: ECEC Phase-2 and Phase-3 Extensions
info: Includes the Chennai-Kanyakumari Industrial Corridor (CKIC) in Tamil Nadu (covering Madurai-Virudhunagar-Dindigul-Theni and Thoothukudi-Tirunelveli nodes) and the Odisha Economic Corridor (OEC, covering Gopalpur-Bhubaneswar-Kalinganagar nodes), tightly integrating domestic manufacturing with Bay of Bengal maritime supply chains.

label: Hyderabad-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor (HBIC)
info: An extension corridor developed across Telangana and Karnataka, centered along NH 44 to create defense, aerospace, pharmaceutical, and electronic hardware clusters. Major anchor node: Orvakal Industrial Area (Kurnool, Andhra Pradesh).

label: Hyderabad-Nagpur Industrial Corridor (HNIC)
info: Traverses northern Telangana and eastern Maharashtra along NH 44; designed to exploit mineral belts, thermal power clusters, and agri-logistics links to central Indian multi-modal hubs like Nagpur (MIHAN).

label: Hyderabad-Warangal Industrial Corridor (HWIC)
info: Concentrated intra-state corridor in Telangana capitalizing on the Kakatiya Mega Textile Park at Warangal and pharmaceutical manufacturing zones outside Hyderabad, supported by rail and expressway connections.

label: Delhi-Nagpur Industrial Corridor (DNIC)
info: A high-capacity north-south economic corridor cutting across Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra, integrating central Indian agro-mineral hinterlands with northern consumer markets.

label: Dedicated Freight Corridors (DFCs) - Strategic Infrastructure Backbone
info: Executed by Dedicated Freight Corridor Corporation of India Limited (DFCCIL) under the Ministry of Railways. Operates heavy-haul, long-formation trains running double-stack container rakes at speeds up to 100 km/h, shifting freight off congested passenger tracks.

label: Western DFC vs. Eastern DFC Specifications
info: Western DFC (1,506 km from Dadri, UP to JNPA, Navi Mumbai) is fully electrified and engineered for double-stack container transit, funded largely by JICA. Eastern DFC (1,875 km from Sahnewal/Ludhiana, Punjab to Dankuni, West Bengal) is specialized for bulk coal, steel, and grain movements, funded largely by the World Bank.

label: Bharatmala Pariyojana - Economic Corridors Component
info: Flagship highway development program of the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways (MoRTH) implemented by NHAI. Earmarks the construction and upgradation of 44 Economic Corridors (~26,000 km) and 24 Inter-Corridors to capture the bulk of long-distance inter-state freight movement.

label: Multi-Modal Logistics Parks (MMLPs)
info: Conceived under MoRTH's Logistics Efficiency Enhancement Programme (LEEP) and National Highways Logistics Management Limited (NHLML) across 35 strategic locations (e.g., Jogighopa in Assam, Nagpur, Indore, Chennai). Feature mechanized warehousing, cold chains, inland container depots (ICDs), and direct rail-road sidings to minimize freight transshipment friction.

label: PM GatiShakti National Master Plan (NMP)
info: Launched in 2021 as a GIS-based digital platform developed with BISAG-N, breaking departmental silos across 16 central infrastructure ministries. Hosts over 1,400 geospatial data layers to synchronize corridor planning, multi-modal alignment, utility relocation, and land clearance.

label: National Logistics Policy (NLP) Synergy
info: Notified by DPIIT in 2022 to complement physical economic corridors with soft infrastructure: driven by the Unified Logistics Interface Platform (ULIP) for seamless cross-modal digital data exchange, Ease of Logistics (ELOG) for grievance redressal, and System Improvement Groups (SIG).

label: Coastal Economic Zones (CEZs) under Sagarmala
info: Economic development zones designated across 14 coastal regions under the Ministry of Ports, Shipping and Waterways. Aligned directly with industrial corridor nodes to promote coastal shipping, export manufacturing, and port-proximate processing (e.g., petrochemicals, electronics, leather).

label: International Trans-Corridor Integration
info: India's domestic economic corridors link into external geopolitical connectivity axes: International North-South Transport Corridor (INSTC via Chabahar/Bandar Abbas to Central Asia/Russia), India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), and the Trilateral Highway/Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Project under the Act East Policy.

label: Key Structural Challenges in Corridor Implementation
info: Prolonged land acquisition delays across high-density agricultural belts, complex Centre-State coordinate friction in finalizing SPV capitalization, underutilized trunk infrastructure in early nodes, environmental clearances across eco-sensitive zones, and ensuring last-mile rail-road siding connectivity for private industrial tenants.
